extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of Plato; scholars and readers of political philosophy and educational theory
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive principles for selecting, testing, educating, and housing the guardian (ruling/auxiliary) class in an ideal city — covering moral character, training (music and gymnastic), lifestyle restrictions, tests, and civic organization. Drawn from Plato's dialogic exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicians should treat only definite ailments
rubrics_metrics.description: The art of medicine should be exhibited only to persons who, being generally of healthy constitution and habits of life, had a definite ailment; such as these he cured by purges and operations, and bade them live as usual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians should not engage in lengthy dieting/regimen to prolong 'good-for-nothing' lives; do not attempt to cure bodies 'which disease had penetrated through and through' as that would be of no use to the individual or the State. Prioritize remedies that allow individuals to resume their occupations; avoid extending lives that offer no benefit to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artisan-appropriate medical practice (practical, brief cures)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a carpenter is ill he asks the physician for a rough and ready cure ... he has no time to be ill, and that he sees no good in a life which is spent in nursing his disease to the neglect of his customary employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical guidance for working people should be pragmatic and oriented to quick return to their trade; avoid imposing extensive regimens that prevent them from fulfilling their occupations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician competence through experience of disease
rubrics_metrics.description: The most skilful physicians are those who, from their youth upwards, have combined with the knowledge of their art the greatest experience of disease; they had better not be robust in health, and should have had all manner of diseases in their own persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians cure 'with the mind' and benefit from direct experience with disease; practical exposure to varied illnesses informs medical judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge suitability: educated, experienced in observing evil (not corrupt)
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge ... ought not therefore to have been trained among vicious minds, and to have associated with them from youth upwards ... The honourable mind which is to form a healthy judgment should have had no experience or contamination of evil habits when young.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good judges should learn of vice through long observation of others rather than personal practice; they should be older and shaped by knowledge, not by personal commission of crimes, so their judgments are guided by virtue and wisdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of guardians based on love of State and repugnance to harming it
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us note among the guardians those who in their whole life show the greatest eagerness to do what is for the good of their country, and the greatest repugnance to do what is against her interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch candidates at every age to see whether they preserve their resolution; select those who consistently prefer the State's good and reject those who fail such tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelong testing of guardians (trials of theft, force, enchantment)
rubrics_metrics.description: We must watch them from their youth upwards, and make them perform actions in which they are most likely to forget or to be deceived ... we must try them with enchantments—that is the third sort of test—and see what will be their behaviour ... pass them into pleasures, and prove them more thoroughly than gold is proved in the furnace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess guardians via staged trials (temptation, fear, pleasure) across life stages to ensure resistance to deception and corruption; only those 'victorious and pure' at every age are appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must have harmonious soul: both temperate and courageous
rubrics_metrics.description: The harmonious soul is both temperate and courageous ... the guardians ought to have both these qualities? Assuredly. And both should be in harmony?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should aim to balance spirited and philosophical elements (via music and gymnastic) so guardians are neither savage nor effeminate but moderate, gentle, and courageous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced education: mixing music and gymnastic
rubrics_metrics.description: He who mingles music with gymnastic in the fairest proportions, and best attempers them to the soul, may be rightly called the true musician and harmonist ... music and gymnastic be preserved in their original form, and no innovation made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train youth in both disciplines to temper spirit and intellect; preserve traditional forms and prohibit innovations that could alter fundamental character and laws of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of musical innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any musical innovation is full of danger to the whole State, and ought to be prohibited ... when modes of music change, the fundamental laws of the State always change with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against new kinds of songs or modes; cultural innovations in music are potentially destabilizing and should be restricted to preserve social order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians' material and domestic restrictions (no private property)
rubrics_metrics.description: None of them should have any property of his own beyond what is absolutely necessary; neither should they have a private house or store closed against any one ... they should agree to receive from the citizens a fixed rate of pay ... Gold and silver we will tell them that they have from God ... they alone of all the citizens may not touch or handle silver or gold ... or be under the same roof with them, or wear them, or drink from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent guardians' accumulation of wealth and private households to avoid corruption, faction, and tyranny; communal mess and modest pay preserve their role as servants of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military-style dwellings and habits for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Their dwellings must be such as will shield them against the cold of winter and the heat of summer ... they must be the houses of soldiers, and not of shop-keepers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design guardians' housing and way of life to sustain military readiness and discipline and to prevent development of domestic wealth or habits that could undermine their civic duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians should be watched for susceptibility to deception or loss of conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a selection. ... We must watch them from their youth upwards, and make them perform actions in which they are most likely to forget or to be deceived, and he who remembers and is not deceived is to be selected, and he who fails in the trial is to be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous observation across ages for steadfastness of conviction; deploy tests that simulate theft of truth (persuasion), force (pain/grief), and enchantment (pleasure/fear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulate births and preserve 'purity' of class via myth and breeding
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall say to them in our tale, you are brothers, yet God has framed you differently. Some ... he has mingled gold ... others he has made of silver ... and the species will generally be preserved in the children ... God proclaims ... that there is nothing which they should so anxiously guard ... as of the purity of the race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a sanctioned myth ('royal lie') to inculcate class loyalty and encourage guardians to preserve class composition; manage marriages and rearing to maintain appropriate dispositions (with allowance for natural transpositions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Social mobility by nature: degrade/elevate offspring according to quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of degrading the offspring of the guardians when inferior, and of elevating into the rank of guardians the offspring of the lower classes, when naturally superior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement mechanisms to promote individuals by natural aptitude and demote where nature dictates; ensure role assignment aligns with natural capacities rather than birth alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit State size to maintain unity and self-sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: I would allow the State to increase so far as is consistent with unity ... Let our city be accounted neither large nor small, but one and self-sufficing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set territorial and population limits so political unity is preserved; expansion only insofar as it does not compromise the single, self-sufficient character of the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against wealth and poverty as degenerative forces
rubrics_metrics.description: There seem to be two causes of the deterioration of the arts. What are they? We alledge: Wealth, and poverty ... When a potter becomes rich, will he ... any longer take the same pains with his art? ... if he has no money ... he will not work equally well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians must watch and counteract the corrupting effects of both excess wealth (luxury, indolence) and extreme poverty (meanness, inability to maintain craft); maintain economic arrangements that prevent degeneration of skills and civic discontent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and nurture as the primary concern
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations which we are prescribing ... are not a number of great principles, but trifles all, if care be taken ... of the one great thing ... Education, I said, and nurture: If our citizens are well educated, and grow into sensible men, they will easily see their way through all these ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize upbringing, musical and gymnastic training, and early formation of habits and manners over heavy-handed legislation; good education produces stable character and improves the polis over generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training young citizens in decorum, manners, and respect
rubrics_metrics.description: When the young are to be silent before their elders; how they are to show respect to them by standing and making them sit; what honour is due to parents; what garments or shoes are to be worn; the mode of dressing the hair; deportment and manners in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage the internalization of social norms and small rules of conduct through early habit rather than detailed codification; these informal practices sustain order and virtue.
